title: Final review of Phase 1 epic diff
description: Review the integrated Phase 1 diff: lease correctness under concurrency and after crash, stop and budget enforcement living in the control plane rather than in a prompt, credential scope of the orchestrator sandbox, gateway telemetry as the cost authority, artifact streaming during the run, and the absence of any mid-run mutation path (D21). Verify against a REAL deployment, not only the test harness - Phase 0 shipped two production breaks that a fully green suite could not see.
notes:
2026-08-20 01:31 - FINAL REVIEW — Phase 1 (ko8), integrated diff main...HEAD = 225 files, +33278/-375 (includes epic 48d, which shares this branch by design).

VERIFIED AGAINST A REAL DEPLOYMENT, as the tick requires — not only the harness:
- tk factory deploy of the full Phase 1 code: exit 0, wrangler resolved by name, D1 and R2 reused (idempotent), verified /health plus one authenticated request.
- Live D1 carries every Phase 1 migration: 0001_init, 0002_runs, 0003_enrolled_projects, 0004_run_gateway_token; tables factory_deployment, runs, signals, dispatch_log, enrolled_project, run_gateway_token. The schema is deployed, not a fixture.
- Live /health: bindings run_rooms/artifacts/db all true, auth required and configured.

AXES THE TICK NAMED:
- LEASE CORRECTNESS — PASS, foundation-reviewed at afj before dependents built on it: compare-and-delete with the token withheld from refused callers, alarm expiry, renewal on same-run re-acquire, bounds-checked ttl refused rather than clamped, local|cloud origin per D19.
- STOP AND BUDGET IN THE CONTROL PLANE, NOT THE PROMPT — PASS. run-workflow.ts states the rule in its own header (an agent can be argued out of a budget, a Workflow step cannot) and implements wall-clock and cost as workflow-level stops. Clean-stop semantics shared with the operator stop path.
- GATEWAY TELEMETRY AS COST AUTHORITY — PASS with one finding, below.
- ARTIFACT STREAMING DURING THE RUN — PASS, and the implementation reasons correctly about the platform: R2 has no append, so the stream is a sequence of immutable segment objects, one PUT per flush. 'A log that ships at exit is a log a crash deletes.'
- NO MID-RUN MUTATION PATH (D21) — PASS, verified by absence: no steer/inject/prompt/message route exists on the run API. Steering is stop, edit the tracker, run again.
- PRE-FLIGHT — PASS after orl: zero markdown parsing left in preflight.sh; the entrypoint asks the verified tk binary, so a migrated repo actually runs its checks instead of silently passing.

FINDING 1 — SHOULD-FIX (high confidence). A run whose gateway cost telemetry is unavailable still STARTS, bounded only by wall clock, with the fact logged and recorded (run-workflow.ts acquireContext: 'Reported, not enforced'). The reasoning is sound as far as it goes — a telemetry outage should not take the factory down, and recording 'cost unknown' beats implying zero spend. But the consequence is that an explicitly configured cost budget silently degrades to wall-clock-only, which is the one budget an operator sets precisely because wall clock does not bound spend on metered keys. Recommend: when a cost budget is explicitly configured and telemetry cannot be read, REFUSE the run with an actionable message; proceed only when no cost budget was set. That keeps the outage-tolerance for the common case and preserves the guarantee for the operator who asked for one.

No blockers. This epic's real defects were all caught earlier by the gate, the foundation review, and live deployment — which is the finding worth carrying into the retro.
closed_reason: Completed: final review of the Phase 1 diff (225 files) against a REAL deployment — live deploy exit 0, all four migrations applied to the live D1, health and auth verified; lease correctness, control-plane budget/stop, artifact streaming during the run, and the absence of any mid-run mutation path all confirmed. One should-fix raised and routed as a repair rather than deferred.
